_note: Fact check of 6 Oct 2026 (Part B step 4): card wording read next to its report entry; each fix only restores the entry's own hedge or cuts a claim the entry does not make. Applied after the stranger check, merged with its fixes.

s3.head: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is reportedly close to raising at least $12 billion.
s3.why: entry: close to securing / raising at least $12 billion; 'set to give' said more than that

s7.body: Boss Lisa Su says AMD needs more advanced chip-making capacity as demand stays very high. She spoke in Taiwan while visiting suppliers, but gave no figures.
s7.why: 'announced no deals' is not in the entry or the facts

s9.body: Jet-powered drones are harder to stop, so these first kills offer a possible answer. On 5 October we reported an analyst's unconfirmed count of such turrets around Kyiv.
s9.why: facts: 'harder to stop' (50 to 70 percent intercepted against over 85 percent of propeller models), not 'the hardest'

s10.body: Start-up Reflection says Beam needs far less computing power; outsiders have not checked this yet. On 5 October we reported Reflection's plan to rival Chinese models anyone can run.
s10.why: entry: claims not independently verified; 'cannot check' is a different claim

s12.body: Ex-Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon said humanity is more likely than not to lose control of AI on the current path. Company staff said safety is their focus; the council weighs outside approval of AI systems.
s12.why: entry: 'on the current path' is the speaker's own condition

t1.head: NATO's top general is drafting a plan to beat a Russian attack using drones and AI.
t1.why: entry: is drafting (due to present 12 Oct), a Russian attack on the eastern flank; 'drafted' and 'any' say more
